_comment: Public log. PRIVACY RULE: never name a reporter, quote their message, or include a Telegram id. Show that reports get fixed, not who reported them. status: fixed | in progress | planned | wont fix. ⚠ Only list PLANNED items you actually intend to build, and never put a DATE on one — a missed date on a public page is a promise broken in writing.

fixes.what: After answering a question that happened to include an image, the button underneath could lock you into image-only questions from then on - even if you never asked for image-only practice. Fixed; the next button now follows the mode you're actually in, not just whatever the last question happened to look like.

New free-tier users could get a message saying their free trial had ended, sometimes after answering a single question. There is no time-limited trial on this bot (never has been on the free tier's daily allowance) - a background message was miscalculating and firing anyway. Fixed; it can no longer send.

A question about semen analysis was keyed to the wrong WHO reference number - it asked for the PROGRESSIVE motility figure (30%) but was keyed to the TOTAL motility figure (42%), a different measurement. One user had already been told the old answer was correct; the key is now fixed and the question is back in the bank.

A question was reported where the options referred to numbered statements that were never actually printed in the question - so there was no way to know what the statements said. Checked, and it was a real gap in the original source, not something that got lost along the way. Scanned every live question for the same pattern (options pointing at a numbered or lettered list that never appears) and found three more the same way. All four are held back rather than guessed at.

449 more questions now carry a written explanation, taking the bank from about 3,900 to 4,400 servable. Every one was checked by independently re-solving it and confirming the answer matched what's stored before the explanation was written — the key itself was never touched. About 70 questions from the same source turned out to be unanswerable as extracted (the printed original referenced a list or a data table that never made it into our copy); those stay held back rather than being explained around, and are now specifically tagged so a future pass through the original books can find all of them at once instead of rediscovering them one at a time.

Twenty-five questions were deleted permanently. These are the ones that had been held out of the bank because they could not be rebuilt honestly — a question whose entire text was "Assessment of resources.", one with four clean options and no question above them, one where a head-injury case had been fused onto four options about urinary chemistry by a bad scan. Every deleted row was written to a file first and read back and compared before anything was removed, and they were taken out of the import files too so a future re-import cannot quietly put them back. The number of questions you can actually practise did not change: none of these was ever being served.

Four answer keys were corrected and the questions put back into the bank. A newborn galactosaemia question was keyed to the wrong enzyme; a forensic question cited the wrong section of the law; a milestones question was keyed "all of the above" when only one of its four statements is true; and a breast cancer staging question was keyed to a stage its own printed staging table contradicts. All four had been held back rather than served while the keys were in doubt, so nobody was ever shown the wrong answer. One more question stays held: it asks which type of gastric ulcer goes with low stomach acid and two of its four options are correct, which no answer key can fix.

Mixed practice was not spreading questions across subjects. It avoided repeating a question you had recently seen, but it never looked at the SUBJECT, so the same subject could come up two or three times in a row — measured at roughly one back-to-back repeat every fifteen questions. Tutor Mode now holds back the last three subjects you were served, so the feed moves through all 19. Picking a subject deliberately still keeps you in that subject.

Exam Mode has a new Custom module. Tick any set of subjects and it builds a timed paper from just those. The questions are split evenly across what you tick rather than by how many the bank happens to hold, so pairing a small subject with a large one gives you half of each instead of a paper that is almost entirely the large one. Between drilling a single subject and sitting the whole syllabus, there was nothing — this is that middle.

Four questions were carrying an advertisement for someone else's app, printed into the question text by the scanner along with the rest of the page. They were live. A search of the whole bank for anything of that kind — app names, links, channel invitations — found those four and nothing else, and all four are clean now. It should never have been possible to read that inside a question you had paid to study from.

Nine questions had the next chapter's heading printed onto the end of their last option — an option that read "Ogive is a cumulative frequency curve. Community Medicine". One of them had been reported as having a wrong answer key. The key was right; the question simply looked untrustworthy, which is a fair reason to doubt it. Alongside these, fourteen questions were repaired where the scan had run words together, including one whose explanation said "Themis match" where the word was "mismatch" — the exact concept that question tests.

Every question that had been withheld from the bank was re-read — thirty-nine of them. Ten went back in, including one whose picture turned out to be a photograph of an entire book page with two unrelated questions in the margin, now cropped to the instrument it was asking about. Three were pulled because their own stated answer disagrees with the reference table printed inside the same question, and those stay out until I can check them against the original paper. The remaining thirty stay out: most of them are missing the question itself, not just an explanation, and a question I cannot rebuild honestly is one I will not serve.

You can now add two extra Grand Tests to an active plan for ₹99, instead of having to buy another whole month to get more mock sittings. It is offered only when you have actually used up the tests your plan includes, it adds tests and nothing else — no extra days, no new plan, nothing renews — and the tests stay valid for 30 days. Because it can only be bought on top of a plan you are already using, it is not covered by the cooling-off refund window; if the tests fail to arrive or do not work, that is still refunded in full. See the Refund Policy for the detail.

416 INI-CET questions were being left out of INI-CET and NEET-PG practice entirely. The filter that decides which questions belong to which exam matched the exam name only at the very start of a question's catalogue entry, and on these 416 the exam name sat one word further along — so they were imported, checked, explained, and then never shown to anyone practising for the exam they came from. They are now in the pool where they always belonged.

The exam tag under a question showed an internal cataloguing note next to the exam name on some questions — something meaningful to me and to nobody else. It now shows the exam and the year only, which is all it was ever meant to say. Nothing about the questions themselves changed, and the original record is kept on my side.

Six questions had the correct answer's text accidentally appended to the end of option D, so the answer was sitting inside a wrong option. Four of them were live. The proper wording for each was read back off the original paper rather than guessed at, and no answer key was changed. The same import fault had also truncated another question's options at a line break and glued the missing halves onto the front of the next question; both are repaired.

Two more reports closed. One was a question the scanner had mangled — words run together, and a vaccine printed with the letter O where a zero belonged, which quietly broke one of the options. The other challenged an answer key: the key was right, but the explanation had been damaged into near-nonsense, which is a perfectly fair reason to doubt it. It has been rewritten. A report that turns out to be a false alarm is still worth sending — this one found a real fault.

Wrote explanations for 68 image-based questions that had none. Each was written after looking at that question's own figure, and each says why the other options are wrong rather than only why the answer is right. They stay held back until their figures have been checked by hand. Also corrected subject labels on questions filed under plainly the wrong subject — a hip dislocation listed under Biochemistry, for one. The cause was an automatic classifier matching fragments of words instead of whole words; it now says it is unsure rather than guessing.

A reader flagged a question and it turned out to be broken four ways — its explanation belonged to a different question, two options were near-identical, and the figure it depends on had never been stored. That one report led to a check of the whole bank, which found 30 more questions where the parser had merged the NEXT question's text into an answer option. 20 of those are now repaired — including one where an option had swallowed a second answer, so restoring it gave the question its missing fourth choice back. 13 are held back until I can rebuild them properly, and the question that was flagged is out of circulation until its figure is in place.

When you tap 'This looks wrong', you're now asked what looked wrong — one tap, six options. Previously a report told me only that something was off, which is hard to act on and impossible to reply to properly. The report still files if you skip the question.

Added Grand Tests — a full-length mock in the real exam's own shape. FMGE is 300 questions across two papers with sections of 50 and no negative marking; NEET-PG and INI-CET are simulated with their own question counts, timing and marking schemes. Two a month on the 1-month and auto-renew plans, and one on the 1-week plan.
The 1-week plan now includes one Grand Test. It previously included none.

Fixed: Grand Tests were not unlocking for everyone entitled to them. Access was being checked against how a plan was recorded rather than how long it runs for, so some people on an active plan were told their plan did not include a Grand Test when it did. Anyone affected now has their full allowance, and nothing was deducted for a test they were refused.

A Grand Test can be paused for a break. The clock stops, and it costs marks — about ten questions' worth — because in the real exam a break costs you time you never get back. The price is shown before you start and again when you tap it.

Got one wrong? Tap 'Why not X?' to see why the option you chose was wrong, taken from the same hand-checked explanation. If the explanation doesn't cover that option, the button isn't offered rather than showing something vague.
Every question now has a one-tap 'This looks wrong' button. It opens a real ticket you can follow with /myfeedback, and it goes straight to me.
You can set your exam date with /examdate and see a countdown on your progress.

You can now tell the bot which exam you're preparing for. FMGE, NEET-PG and INI-CET stay together on purpose — they overlap heavily and practising across all three is what builds exam-day speed. UPSC CMS and university subject exams are being built; you can join the list for either and I'll message you the day it opens.
The free plan now gives 5 questions a day instead of 3, and one of them is always an image-based question with the real figure.

Added a safeguard against paying twice. If you already have access, or you opened a payment page in the last few minutes, the bot stops and tells you to check /myplan first rather than letting you pay again.
Corrected the checkout wording. It said access unlocks 'instantly'; it now says access unlocks automatically, usually within seconds and always within a few minutes, which is what actually happens.

The leaderboard now has three boards: most answered, best accuracy, and longest streak. The old single board ranked only by volume, which nobody on the free plan could ever top. Accuracy and streak are winnable by anyone.
Opening the bot now starts you on a real question straight away instead of showing a page of description first.

Added an optional daily reminder. Pick a time and get one short message a day, plus a summary of your week on Sundays. It is off unless you choose a time, it is never more than one message a day, and every reminder carries a one-tap Turn off button.
Added a shareable progress card — your questions answered, accuracy, streak and rank as a single image you can post. Get it with /mycard or from Progress.
Every question now shows which exam and year it came from, for example 'NEET-PG 2023'. Two older sets have no year recorded, so those show the exam alone rather than a guessed year.
Fixed 6 questions where OCR had duplicated one of the options, so the same choice appeared twice. The correct answer was never affected; the repeated option has been removed.
Reorganised the buttons under the message box. They are now grouped into Practice and My Account instead of one long list, so the menu takes up less of the screen while you are reading a question.
My Plan and Help can now be reached from the menu itself, under My Account. Previously you had to already know the command existed to check your own plan or find help.

Subscription payments were not unlocking access. A payment made through the auto-renew plan was not being linked back to the buyer's account, so access stayed locked. Fixed the same day; affected payment refunded in full and access granted.
Added /myplan so anyone can check their own plan, expiry and auto-renew status without asking.
Added UPI QR as a payment option alongside the card/UPI link.

Corrected OCR damage across 780+ questions: glued-together words, Roman numerals misread as lowercase letters (CN Vll to CN VII, Angiotensin ll to II), and stray source-book page references left inside explanations.
Removed one question whose patient age was clearly corrupted. It is out of rotation until it can be checked against the source.
Corrected the advertised question counts to match what the bot actually serves, and stated the number of image questions still held back.
Six questions carry a duplicated answer option. The correct answer is unaffected in every case; the duplicate distractor is being replaced.

planned.why: Right now the bot runs on my own laptop, so it can only answer while that machine is awake. Nothing is ever lost — messages queue and payments are picked up automatically — but you can be left waiting. A proper server ends that.
planned.when: Subscriptions cover the monthly server cost

planned.why: Access already unlocks by itself, usually in seconds. On a server with a fixed address the confirmation is immediate and never depends on my laptop being on.
planned.when: The move to always-on hosting is done

planned.goal: The questions that are still missing their figure
planned.why: Every image question the bot serves today carries its own figure — none are held back mid-flight any more. What is left is a smaller set that never made it into the bank at all, because the figure they depend on could not be read clearly enough to be sure of the answer. Those stay out until I can crop and check each one by hand.
planned.when: Ongoing — a batch at a time

planned.goal: The last of the OCR damage cleaned up
planned.why: A tail of run-together words still sits in some explanations. Nothing here affects an answer key — it is readability only — and it is being fixed by hand rather than by a script, because an automated fix on medical text does more harm than good.
planned.when: Ongoing — a batch at a time

planned.why: Both are already in the bank and both keep growing. FMGE is the deepest today; the aim is for all three to feel equally complete.
planned.when: Ongoing — questions are added every week

planned.goal: Other medical entrance and service exams, starting with UPSC CMS
planned.why: One place to practise whichever exam you are sitting, rather than a different app for each.
planned.when: The three current exams are where I want them
